lines: Mark Cuban argues US healthcare's core problem is missing price discovery and broken incentives, and that AI alone won't fix it; transparency is the most effective disruptive tool.

His immediate advice for employers: run every benefits contract through AI before signing to expose hidden fees and intercompany transfers, which he calls 'contractual terrorism' by vertically integrated carriers steering plans to their own high-cost subsidiaries.

He says Cost Plus Drugs' public, low-markup pricing has pushed incumbents to cut prices even without direct deals, and proposes mandatory disclosure of taxpayer-funded contracts and letting cheaper out-of-network care count toward deductibles.

Cuban sees modular, trailer-sized manufacturing pods enabling local production of sterile injectables and personalized 'end-of-one' therapies, with DNA-based medicine becoming a subscription service as AI pushes drug design costs toward zero.
He expects doctors to become physician-scientists using AI on patient-specific data, and argues companies need C-suites that understand how models work to stay competitive.
title: Mark Cuban’s Plan to Make Healthcare Affordable
